name: Gravis Robotics Gravis Rack
summary: A roof-mounted sensor and computer kit with a tablet that lets excavators and wheel loaders of 10 to 100+ tons dig trenches, load trucks and grade on their own, or guide the operator in the cab.

germany.statusNote: On request from Zürich: Gravis offers its kit and Gravis-equipped machines for rental or purchase through dealers and rental partners and works in Switzerland, the UK and the EU. No German customer, dealer or price named yet. The Develon-integrated version (Real X) reached its first European customer, KIBAG in Switzerland, through the Swiss Develon dealer.

sellers.name: Gravis Robotics AG
sellers.note: Headquarters Zürich, offices in Austin (USA) and Oxford (UK). Offers turnkey rental and purchase of Gravis-equipped machines through local dealers and rental providers; select machine models supported by dealer integration. Price on request.

specs.label: Host machines
specs.conditions: trucks, dozers, forklifts and graders not supported

specs.label: Machine size
specs.conditions: rack sizes S, M, L, XL

specs.label: Machine brands
specs.value: installed on a dozen brands, including Caterpillar, Case, Develon, John Deere, JCB, Hitachi, Sumitomo, Yanmar and Volvo

specs.label: Machine requirement
specs.value: electro-hydraulic (EH) pilot control; machines with mechanical pilot valves need a retrofit EH valve

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: front camera and LiDAR; rear masts with GNSS RTK, wide-angle HDR cameras, 3D LiDAR and long-range WiFi; surround-view cameras

specs.label: Operator interface
specs.value: Slate tablet with integrated wireless stop; in-cab copilot, field command or remote supervision of one or more machines

specs.label: Job input
specs.value: geometry from CAD/BIM models, or reference points set on site by touch, bucket or XYZ values

specs.label: Dumping
specs.value: spoil pile, hopper or truck (truck position detected by the AI)

notes: Retrofit kit: the crawler excavator or wheel loader and its bucket come from the customer, a dealer or a rental firm.
Modes range from in-cab assistance to full autonomy supervised from outside the cab or remotely.
In the UK trial a trained machine controller is the only person allowed to start the work and can stop the machine at any time.
Rules for fully autonomous machines on public sites are still missing; KIBAG runs its machine on private land under technical supervision.

images.alt: Gravis Rack sensor and computer unit with GNSS masts on a machine cab roof

evidence.task: Showed autonomous truck loading, tap-to-dig trenching and remote autonomy of an excavator 300 km away, with several machine makers
A 23-tonne Develon crawler excavator with Gravis technology fed a screener hopper with sand and gravel for two days, averaging 133 cycles an hour and about 1,500 tonnes a day
evidence.where: Holcim UK, Lee Moor sand and gravel quarry, Plymouth, UK

evidence.task: A Yanmar SV100-7 excavator with the Gravis kit dug trenches to pipe-laying standard from a 3D model and skipped the section where the model showed existing pipes
evidence.where: Taylor Woodrow, Clough Bank B car park, Manchester Airport, UK
evidence.note: Trial on 21 October 2025 ahead of use on the live site.

evidence.task: A Develon crawler excavator with Gravis control digs a 150 m long, 17 m wide and 3 m deep trench without an operator
evidence.note: Pilot running since autumn 2025 and planned until at least summer 2026; KIBAG reports the programming took more effort than expected.

evidence.task: KIBAG took over a Develon Real X DX225LC (developed with Gravis, Gravis Rack on the roof) to dig a 300 m long, 6 m wide, 3 m deep trench for slope stabilisation
evidence.where: KIBAG, former quarry in Tuggen, Switzerland
evidence.note: First European customer of the Develon-integrated version, supplied through the Swiss Develon dealer AG für Baumaschinen Schmerikon.

evidence.task: Autonomous excavator shown to about 900 dealers, customers and journalists
evidence.where: Develon Demo Days, Prague, Czech Republic
